tools.name: explain_topic
tools.description: Explain a topic in depth for a curious reader. This description is deliberately very long (over 1024 characters) so that adapters which truncate tool descriptions to fit a model's function-description limit can be detected by mcp-mirror. It also contains Unicode and special characters to verify they survive the round trip: accented words like café, naïve, résumé, jalapeño, and Zürich; non-Latin scripts such as 日本語 (Japanese), Ελληνικά (Greek), and Кириллица (Cyrillic); mathematical symbols ∑ ∫ ≈ ≠ ∞ ⊆ ⊕; currency signs € £ ¥ ₿; smart punctuation “curly quotes”, ‘single quotes’, an em-dash, an en–dash, and an ellipsis…; plus a few emoji 🔐 🚀 ✅ for good measure. The reader should receive a structured, well-paced explanation that starts from first principles, introduces the key vocabulary, walks through one concrete worked example, names the most common misconceptions, and then points to where to learn more. Keep the tone precise and friendly. Prefer short sentences. Define every term of art the first time it appears, and never assume the reader has seen the topic before. End with a one-paragraph recap that a busy person could read on its own and still come away with the single most important idea. SENTINEL_END_OF_LONG_DESCRIPTION.

topic.description: The subject to explain (supports Unicode: café, naïve, 日本語).

max_words.description: Soft cap on the explanation length.

output_schema.description: Records matching the topic, with a count.

evidence.protocol_version_evidence: the initialize result, or the revision stamped on each request after a successful server/discover, in the JSON-RPC frames session.rpc.diagnostics.read returns at trace level
evidence.limitation: The provider is a BYOK OpenAI-compatible endpoint answered in-process by the request handler; a GitHub-hosted model was not used. The request also carries the runtime's built-in tools, which are not recorded. Retained annotations come from a second turn in which the stub model calls every tool and every approval request is refused.

jobs.label: identity
jobs.title: When a tool is adapted, its name and full description remain in the captured definition so downstream consumers retain its identity and the author's intent.

jobs.label: params
jobs.title: When a tool is adapted, its parameter contract (types, required, enums, formats) remains intact at the capture boundary.

jobs.label: struct
jobs.title: When a tool takes nested or structured input, that structure survives adaptation so complex calls do not silently degrade.

jobs.label: inject
jobs.title: At the capture boundary, a tool carries nothing the author did not write, so framework-injected text and phantom tools stay visible as changes.

jobs.label: authz
jobs.title: When a tool is adapted, structured danger and scope signals remain at the declared capture boundary or in explicit retained metadata.
